entries.description: Target cost-control architecture for controlled-live integrations (AUDIT OUTPUT, DESIGNED - NOT YET IMPLEMENTED): per live provider - Provider; credential status; plan; entitlement; allowance (free+paid); usage (request count, last success, last error, cost); remaining allowance; Mercenta safety cap (configurable, per-provider); cache status; data freshness; auto-stop (fail-closed on cap, simulation fallback); health. Rules: (1) a configured credential must NOT by itself trigger live traffic; (2) reaching the Mercenta safety cap STOPS live requests, fails closed, uses simulation fallback, never silently creates paid usage; (3) repeated identical data is cached/deduplicated; (4) no needless polling. Existing partial controls to EXTEND (not replace): DISCOVERY_BUDGET_CAPS_PLACEHOLDER_GBP (GBP in-memory caps), AI_SPEND_CEILINGS + usageLog (AI daily/monthly ceilings + per-call log), per-crawl GBP charge, idempotent payout mock ledger, usageLog cache_hit. GAPS found: no credit-aware caps (Hunter 50/mo, Firecrawl allowances), no persistent usage ledger (in-memory only), no provider entitlement metadata, no per-provider request counters surfaced, no Hunter/Firecrawl dedup caches, no auto-stop wired to free allowances.

entries.description: REAL DEFECT FIXED. The returns warehouse flow generated its forward tracking number with `Math.floor(1000 + Math.random() * 9000)`, so the same forward produced a different number on every run — a non-deterministic workflow that could never be reproduced on reload. The suffix is now derived deterministically from the tracking record's own id. The row click's `selectedId` state, which was written but never read (a dead interaction), now drives the record drawer, and a mutation stamp keeps the metric band, filter and drawer reading the CURRENT record after a stage advance.

entries.description: Phase 15 — conversion launch gate: form validation, spam protection, submission reliability, the primary CTA and the Partner Login hierarchy. ALL FOUR PARTS ARE NOW DONE. The CTA hierarchy was done in Phase 1 ("Explore UK Market Fit" is the primary hero CTA and Partner Login is a separate header utility action). SESSION 36 (2026-09-26) closed the remainder — 'spam protection and submission reliability remain' — and the gaps were verified ABSENT in the code BEFORE implementing: no honeypot, no rate limit and no duplicate rule existed anywhere in the public path; the submit handler had no try/catch (a throw left the button stuck on '...' with no message and no reset); the real link verification (10s per link, CORS-blocked for most hosts) ran INSIDE the submit handler, so it held the applicant open; a double submit could record two applications; and validation was three checks with parseInt() turning a non-numeric product count into NaN. NOW: ONE SSOT (src/config/partnerApplication.ts) declares the honeypot, the minimum fill time, the session attempt budget, the duplicate window, the field limits, the country list and every applicant-facing sentence; ONE pure fail-closed decision owner (src/lib/onboarding/applicationGuard.ts) validates and decides with an INJECTED clock and zero network; the store (src/data/applicationStore.ts) counts REFUSED attempts too, enforces the duplicate fail-safe at the DOMAIN boundary and patches verification after the record exists; the form (src/components/auth/PartnerApplicationForm.tsx) renders the honeypot unannounced and unfocusable, shows a per-field announced refusal (aria-invalid + role=alert + focus), stops a double click with a synchronous ref, cannot leave the button stuck (try/catch/finally) and records the application BEFORE the third-party check runs. NOTE: the phone field's '*' marker was REMOVED because the label claimed a requirement the domain never enforced (BrandApplication.phone is nullable); it is now labelled (optional) — making a phone COMPULSORY is a commercial decision for the Founder, not a defect fix. PHONE — NOW COMPULSORY (Founder decision, 2026-09-26): the phone moved from OPTIONAL to REQUIRED. An empty, whitespace-only, separator-only or non-string answer is REFUSED as missing_phone and NOTHING is recorded; the accepted payload and the stored record are NON-NULLABLE (NormalisedApplication.phone, BrandApplication.phone and submitApplication's input contract are all `string`); the form labels the field with a required '*', no longer says (optional), and writes the country's declared dialling code + the applicant's digits; and the reviewer can now READ the number on the application card (ApplicationsPanel showed SKUs/Revenue/Submitted only, so a compulsory number would have been collected and hidden). REPOINTED in the same pass: the sentence above records the OPPOSITE contract (the '*' removed because the domain did not enforce a phone) — the invariant is the same one, label matches domain, now pointed at the new source of truth.

entries.description: §CG (2026-09-26, session 36) — the conversion gate's three capabilities, now owned by declared code rather than by scattered inline checks. VALIDATION: every answer is validated in ONE place against the SSOT limits (company-name length, a country the form actually offers, URL format and host family per link, phone digits, integer product count, per-field and total payload ceilings) — previously three checks plus parseInt() (so a non-numeric count became NaN) and no format check at all. SPAM PROTECTION: four deterministic signals — an off-screen unannounced honeypot, a minimum fill time, a session attempt budget that counts REFUSED attempts, and a duplicate window over RECORDED applications only (so a retry after a refusal is never falsely told 'already received'). No CAPTCHA and no reputation score is claimed: neither is available without an external provider, and inventing one would be a lie. SUBMISSION RELIABILITY: the application is recorded BEFORE the real third-party link check runs (that check previously held the applicant open for up to 10s per link and is CORS-blocked for most hosts), every refusal has an honest declared sentence, the button can no longer be left stuck (try/catch/finally), and a double click cannot record two applications (a synchronous ref plus a DOMAIN-boundary fail-safe). FAIL CLOSED: a missing, non-string, non-finite or malformed signal is a REFUSAL, never a silent acceptance.

entries.description: Exclusive gateway (XOR): exactly one route is selected; it REFUSES rather than defaulting when no condition holds, when more than one holds (ambiguity), when a condition cannot be evaluated (fail-closed), or when the gateway definition itself is malformed (undeclared route, unrouted condition, duplicate route, contradiction). A refusal is never reported as terminal completion
entries.source: Phase 2 — explicit workflow routing / gateway architecture (2026-09-19)
entries.evidence: src/lib/routing/gateways.ts; evaluateExclusiveGateway; validated in the XOR section

entries.description: Parallel gateway (AND): every branch is evaluated independently with its own outcome; a failing branch never erases a sibling branch success; a branch whose sequential prerequisite is unmet does not run and says so
entries.source: Phase 2 — explicit workflow routing / gateway architecture (2026-09-19)
entries.evidence: src/lib/routing/gateways.ts; evaluateParallelGateway; validated in the AND branch-isolation section

entries.description: Inclusive gateway (OR): the selected subset is exactly the set of conditions that held — never exactly-one and never always-all; an explicitly-false condition marks its route not_applicable with the reason; nothing applicable refuses
entries.source: Phase 2 — explicit workflow routing / gateway architecture (2026-09-19)
entries.evidence: src/lib/routing/gateways.ts; evaluateInclusiveGateway; validated in the OR section

entries.description: Fan-in/join with declared completion conditions (all / declared_subset / quorum / any), required vs optional branches, a declared quorum that is never invented, and explicit states (waiting/satisfied/failed/blocked_human_review). Completion is never inferred from the initiating operation, and timed-out or human-review branches never count
entries.source: Phase 2 — explicit workflow routing / gateway architecture (2026-09-19)

entries.description: Credential vault (T-7 / matrix D16-05) — the durable credential architecture. BUILT (2026-10-08): the ONE owner `src/config/credentialVault.ts` DERIVES one contract per integration provider from the canonical registry (which are OAuth or API-key and which secret fields each requires — the fields are REUSED, never re-declared) and declares the vault status vocabulary, the MASK policy, the entry / replacement / secure-persistence / masked-readback / validation / enable-disable RULES and the pinned invariants. The pure fail-closed resolver `src/lib/integrations/resolveCredentialVault.ts` decides when a credential may be USED: it is usable ONLY when the provider is declared, a value is STORED, the credential is ENABLED, every required secret field is present AND the store is DURABLE — an unknown provider, no stored value, a disabled credential, a missing field and a NON-DURABLE store are ALL refused, and only a MASK is ever read back (the value never leaves). The durable store is the injected ACTIVATION seam: the in-memory store the integration layer holds today is NOT durable, so NO provider resolves as a production credential until it is wired (an infrastructure step, never a credential).

entries.description: The canonical operational type scale, which fixes the measured taste debt (finding D-2) AT THE ROOT. The debt was 1,202 arbitrary sub-12px sizes across 113 files (`text-[8px]` 47 · `text-[9px]` 206 · `text-[10px]` 949) plus 644 `text-[11px]` — and the root cause was a design-system failure, not 1,202 mistakes: no NAMED operational size existed below `text-xs`, so every author invented one. `tailwind.config.js` now declares `text-ds-micro` (11px FLOOR) · `text-ds-label` (12px) · `text-ds-body` (13px) · `text-ds-title` (15px) · `text-ds-page` (20px). Migration is mechanical and IDEMPOTENT (1,845 replacements across 116 files; re-run = 0 changes, proven). The gate FAILS on a reappearing micro size, on a missing token, on a floor below 11px, and on a token that is declared but never consumed. A validator BLIND SPOT was found and closed: the first run — and the first validator — both skipped `.jsx`, so the gate reported PASS while `PublicFooterTmp1.jsx` still carried a micro size; both now scan `.ts/.tsx/.jsx/.js/.css`

entries.description: Workspace hierarchy + density, applied platform-wide through the SHARED primitive `WorkspaceHeader` (composed by every migrated surface), plus two REAL defects fixed. (a) STICKY TOOLBAR DEFECT: the offset was `top-[52px]` but the app bar is `h-14` (56px) AND `<main>` is its own scroll container — so the toolbar stuck 52px down inside that scrollport and content visibly scrolled through the band above it. `top-0` is correct because `<main>` already begins below the app bar. (b) METRIC HIERARCHY DEFECT: metric values were `text-xl` (20px) — EXACTLY the page-title size — so a KPI number competed with the `h1` at the same weight; hero values were arbitrary `text-[26px] sm:text-[30px]`. Now hero 24px / default 18px, both BELOW the 20px title while still dominating their row (mono + semibold + white). Title `sm:text-2xl` (24px) → `text-ds-page` (20px) so a serif `h1` reads as an enterprise entity title rather than a marketing headline; description `text-sm` (14px) → `text-ds-body` (13px) so the title clearly wins the first glance; rhythm tightened

entries.description: A UX defect fixed WITHOUT breaking the suite, after the browser suite caught a regression this session caused. The header control rendered the visible text "Home" while actually calling `signOut()` (title: "Back to homepage"), so an innocent-looking navigation label silently destroyed the session. The first attempt REMOVED the control; `e2e/record-drawer.spec.ts:219` then timed out on `getByTitle("Back to homepage")` — FOUR specs drive the exit-to-public-site path through that title (`access-gate:175`, `homepage-editor:77`, `onboarding-workflow:68`, `record-drawer:219`) and it is the only in-shell route back to the public site. Correct remedy: the control is RESTORED with an honest visible label ("Exit to site") plus a `LogOut` icon, `title` retained (it accurately describes the action and is the specs contract), and NO `aria-label` so the accessible name remains identical to the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). Typecheck and build cannot catch this class of defect; only the browser suite did

entries.description: INVESTIGATED in Wave 0 (2026-09-22) against the full-redesign directive §24 ('remove only if it exists SOLELY to support the retired theme'). FINDING: it does NOT. `src/theme-alpha-shims.css` is the Tailwind 3.4 alpha-modifier compatibility layer for the SHARED token palette — Tailwind cannot compute `/opacity` on CSS-variable colours, so it emits explicit `color-mix(in srgb, var(--mr-*), <alpha>, transparent)` rules for the variable-based classes used across the whole product. Deleting it would remove alpha styling from ~215 call sites in the NEW design system, i.e. remove working functionality. Retained, with semantic purpose (motion/density/alpha tokens) intact; the retired theme is not what it supports.

entries.description: DISCOVERED by a build output: the `AdminShell` chunk was 1,010 kB (263 kB gzip) and the build warned about it, because the admin shell imported all ~34 admin view panels EAGERLY. entries.description: P3 live verification found and fixed a PRODUCTION-ONLY mount crash that typecheck, lint, build and the whole browser suite could not see, because the suite runs against the Vite DEV server (unbundled). On the deployed bundle the root element was EMPTY and the app never mounted. Root cause: the manualChunks split made `vendor-react` (recharts) and `vendor-other` (lodash/reselect) import EACH OTHER, so recharts' MODULE-LEVEL calls ran before their imports had initialised - first `TypeError: createSelector is not a function` (reselect), then, after moving the recharts family into vendor-react, `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'gO' before initialization`. The cycle is inherent to splitting a cyclic dependency graph. FIX: one `vendor` chunk for ALL of node_modules (a single instance of React, scheduler and every helper; a cycle cannot span one module) while app code still splits normally. NEW PERMANENT GATE: scripts/validate-production-boot.mjs (npm run validate:production-boot) builds, serves dist over a built-in static server, loads it in Chromium and asserts the app actually MOUNTS (#root non-empty, no page/console error, the Partner Login entry renders) - exit 1 when it does not. Proven to fail on the pre-fix bundle (exit 1, 'TypeError: createSelector is not a function') and pass on the fixed bundle (exit 0).

entries.description: DISCOVERED AND FIXED (2026-09-23, session 16, P4). Building the instruction-to-Mercenta record exposed a data-semantics defect that would have silently disabled fulfilment: `PurchaseOrderLineItem.ackStatus` is OPTIONAL, and seeded/legacy POs carry a terminal status (`accepted` / `ready_to_fulfil`) with NO per-line acknowledgement. The first P4 mapping treated an absent `ackStatus` as a REJECTION, so such a PO issued an all-rejected instruction, Mercenta correctly filed no shipment, and the brand saw 'nothing to ship' for an order it had genuinely accepted. It failed only in a real browser run against seeded data - typecheck, lint and every domain-level validator passed. FIX: ONE shared derivation, `instructionLineFor(po, line)` in src/lib/commerce/channelInstructions.ts - a line that positively says accepted/rejected/backordered keeps it; a PO whose status is `rejected` derives rejected; any other line of a live PO derives ACCEPTED with its ordered quantity. Used by the acknowledgement writer (src/data/api.ts), the brand and admin surfaces and the processor, and asserted in scripts/validate-proxy-model.mjs both against the seeded regression PO and against a synthetic rejected PO.

entries.description: PO-ACK S4 (2026-09-25, session 29) — THE ON-BEHALF REJECTION DRAFT, AND THE BRAND'S APPROVAL THAT EXECUTES IT: THE S2 WRITER FINALLY HAS ITS PRODUCER. Founder directive: the Amazon purchase-order process is a REPLICA of Amazon's documented rules; Mercenta invents nothing. (1) THE DRAFT IS DERIVED BY THE RULE'S OWNER: src/lib/commerce/poAcknowledgementWindow.ts -> poOnBehalfRejectionDraft(po, now?) returns the draft's CONTENT — every line rejected with the channel's documented reason (config-owned PO_ACK_AUTO_REJECT_REASON), the rule in its own words (PO_ACK_WINDOW_RULE_TEXT), both instants (the 24-hour limit and the earlier on-behalf stage), and a CONTENT ADDRESS (`digest`, FNV-1a, pure — no crypto) so an approval is bound to the exact draft that was shown. Availability IS the owner's own predicate (`poNeedsAutoRejection` = Amazon's `New` set at/after the on-behalf instant), so the draft is offered exactly when the S2 writer will perform the rejection: the CLOSING window AND PAST the limit (the documented action past the limit IS a rejection, with brandMayStillDecide: false stating the brand's own decision has closed); everything else FAILS CLOSED with a stated refusal (not yet due — naming the instant; already decided; no obligation; unreadable order date). (2) THE PRODUCER: src/data/api.ts -> draftOnBehalfRejection(poId, now?) records only what is NOT derivable — the content address and the ATTRIBUTION (produced BY PO_ACK_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, FOR the brand whose PO it is) — with ONE canonical audit entry (purchase_order_on_behalf_draft_created) naming the window; IDEMPOTENT (the same content never records a second draft, so a surface may ask on every render) and it PERFORMS NOTHING (the PO is untouched by drafting). A draft whose content changed supersedes the previous one and names the superseded draft in its audit entry, so history is never destroyed. (3) THE APPROVAL IS THE ONLY PATH THAT EXECUTES: src/data/api.ts -> approveOnBehalfRejection(poId, approval, now?) enforces, in order: unknown PO -> TENANT ISOLATION (an actorBrandId that is not the PO's own brand is refused, fail-closed) -> IDEMPOTENCY (a PO that already carries a decision is never re-decided) -> the owner's availability -> a draft MUST be on record -> the recorded digest MUST equal the CURRENT derivation (a PO that changed after drafting cannot be approved blind) -> the approval's draftId MUST be the draft on record -> and only then does it call the S2 writer autoRejectPurchaseOrderOnBehalf. Every refusal leaves the PO byte-for-byte unchanged. The approval is attributed to the acting human ON THE RECORD (approvedBy / approvedAt, plus approvedByAdmin for Mercenta staff) and audited ONCE (purchase_order_on_behalf_rejection_approved) with the draft id, its digest, the actor, the instruction the rejection was issued as, and whether the approval happened inside or after the window; the execution stays attributed separately to the writer's own purchase_order_auto_rejected entry, so the trail shows BOTH facts: WHO approved and WHO performed. (4) BOTH PO SURFACES CARRY THE REAL CONTROL: the brand PO surface (src/components/brand/BrandPurchaseOrders.tsx) shows Mercenta's draft (the rule, the reason code, the draft id, both instants, every line it rejects) and approves it as the brand (actorBrandId = its own tenant, so a cross-tenant approval is impossible); the admin PO detail (src/components/admin/AdminPurchaseOrderDetail.tsx) shows the SAME draft and records the approval as an ATTRIBUTED MERCENTA OVERRIDE; each surface PRODUCES the draft through the idempotent api call in an effect and renders the owner's derivation — neither re-derives the window, the reason code or the instants. (5) THE SEED MAKES IT REACHABLE (src/data/demoData.ts): the second open PO of the first cleared tenant (Astonish PO-9001) is dated into its closing window (deadline minus 1h 30m, arithmetic owned by the declared PO_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_HOURS minus PO_ACK_ON_BEHALF_WINDOW_HOURS), staying INSIDE the 24-hour limit so the brand's own decision remains valid alongside the draft. (6) TWO NEW GATES: scripts/validate-po-acknowledgement-on-behalf.mjs (48 assertions, 0 network calls) and e2e/po-onbehalf.spec.ts (3 functional tests). RECORDED, NOT A BLOCKER: the draft is not yet fanned out to the brand's channels (S5 — today it is materialised when a PO surface reads the PO); an UNATTENDED sweep that rejects without an approval is S5/S10 and needs the founder's decision on the trigger; three legacy inline countdowns still hand-roll the 24-hour arithmetic (BrandPurchaseOrders -> AckDeadline, AdminPurchaseOrderDetail, AdminPurchaseOrderList -> PoPreviewBody) — S6/S7 scope, NOT on S4's code path.

entries.description: PO-ACK S5 (2026-09-25, session 30) - THE ALL-CHANNEL NOTIFICATION FAN-OUT, AND THE INSTANT-MESSAGE SEAM: THE DECLARED SCHEDULE FINALLY REACHES THE BRAND. Founder directive: the Amazon purchase-order process is a REPLICA of Amazon's documented rules; Mercenta invents nothing. (1) THE FAN-OUT OWNER: NEW src/lib/commerce/poAcknowledgementNotifications.ts. The plan is PURE (poAckNotificationPlan: the owner's own stages x the brand's own channels, plus one refusal per channel it cannot use, each with its reason) and the sweep is EXPLICIT (no setInterval/setTimeout/randomness; the caller clock, the same seam the window owner takes). CHANNELS come from the brand's OWN declared NotificationPreference for the acknowledgement event (a disabled or empty preference yields NO channels, and a brand with no preference record yields none either - the platform never invents a subscription). DESTINATIONS come from canonical records and are never invented: in_app is internal (Mercenta operates it), email is the brand's declared contact email (DemoBrand.email, delivered through the platform's own mail adapter, mock-first and labelled simulated from its mock:msg- reference), sms is the brand's declared instant-message number (the brand row's profile.phone; DemoBrandRow.profile is widened to carry it and the demo sets it for nobody). A missing destination returns null and is NEVER defaulted to a plausible fake address. (2) THE EXTERNAL INSTANT-MESSAGE SEAM IS DECLARED AND FAILS CLOSED: a provider is simulated ONLY when its mode POSITIVELY resolves simulation (isProviderSimulationSafe); available/configuring/degraded/error/disabled/unknown/not_registered REFUSE the send and NAME the mode (the refusal states that an unverified provider is never treated as simulation). resolveInstantMessageClient is the ONE factory: the deterministic synchronous mock (MOCK-IM-..., zero network) for simulation, the real Twilio-backed adapter (src/lib/whatsapp/whatsAppClient.ts) for live, and NOTHING for anything else. A live send is genuinely asynchronous, so the delivery is recorded as dispatching and completed when the provider answers - never mistaken for a completed send. (3) THE CANONICAL DELIVERY LEDGER: every delivery and refusal is recorded under the deterministic key po-ack-notify-<poId>-<stage>-<channel> and made AT MOST ONCE, EVER - so a MISSED sweep still owes and delivers every stage reached, and a repeat sweep delivers nothing twice (a refusal whose reason is unchanged is not re-recorded; the moment a channel becomes usable the owed message IS delivered and the superseded refusal is named in the audit entry). No refusal is silent: each carries its reason. (4) THE FINAL STAGE PRODUCES THE DRAFT: when the owner's poNeedsAutoRejection says the rejection is Mercenta's to perform, the sweep invokes S4's producer (draftOnBehalfRejection), so the on-behalf draft exists because the SCHEDULE reached its final stage - not because a surface rendered the purchase order. NOTHING is performed by it, and the gate asserts the purchase order is still undecided afterwards. PAST the limit the schedule does NOT replay 12/6/2 reminders (the brand's decision has closed) - only the required rejection is owed. (5) IT RUNS THROUGH THE EXISTING AUTOMATION SEAM: new automation id po_acknowledgement_fanout, declared ONCE as PO_ACK_NOTIFICATION_AUTOMATION_ID and consumed by the registry's type, order, definition, digest and runner, so the Founder Control Centre gains a REAL Run control with no UI work. resetAutomationStore now also clears the fan-out ledger (fanoutDeliveriesCleared), because the registry's reset returns the platform to its initial state and a delivery is made at most once ever. (6) THE IN-APP CHANNEL REACHES ITS READER: src/components/shared/NotificationCenter.tsx lists the delivered reminders through the tenant-scoped poAckInAppDeliveries(scope, tenantId) accessor (the SAME ledger the fan-out writes, never a second notification store) with the channel and the stage on each item; tenant scoping is enforced INSIDE the domain accessor and fails closed for a brand scope with no tenant. (7) ATTRIBUTION AND AUDIT: the SENDER is Mercenta's declared identity (PO_ACK_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID - Mercenta operates the retail-channel relationship, so the reminder is Mercenta's message on the brand's behalf) and the TRIGGER is the actor who invoked the fan-out; every delivery/refusal produces ONE canonical audit entry (purchase_order_ack_notification_sent / _failed / _refused) and ONE canonical event (po_acknowledgement_notification, added to the EXISTING union). (8) THE SEED MAKES THE EXTERNAL CHANNEL REACHABLE: exactly ONE brand (Astonish, whose PO-9001 sits in the closing window) declares an instant-message subscription for the acknowledgement event, so the fan-out genuinely ATTEMPTS the external channel and REFUSES it with the refusal attributed and audited - no demo brand or account removed.

entries.description: PO-ACK S6 (2026-09-25, session 31) - THE BRAND SURFACES PRESENT THE RULE FROM ITS ONE OWNER, AND THE DELIVERED REMINDER CARRIES ITS OWN CHANNEL DETAIL. Founder directive: the Amazon purchase-order process is a REPLICA of Amazon's documented rules; Mercenta invents nothing. (1) THE BRAND SURFACE CONSUMES THE RULE'S OWNER. src/components/brand/BrandPurchaseOrders.tsx carried FOUR hand-rolled copies of the 24-hour rule (the S4 record listed three and MISSED one). All four are repointed onto src/lib/commerce/poAcknowledgementWindow.ts: (a) AckDeadline was 'received + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000' plus its own Math.ceil hoursLeft - it now reads poAcknowledgementWindow(po) and renders the presentation owner's own urgency (ackDeadlinePresentation(window.hoursLeft)) with the owner's reason as the badge title, renders NOTHING for an acknowledged/closed PO (the owner's own classification) and states 'Ack window unreadable' - FAIL-CLOSED - for an unreadable order date (the old code rendered 'Ack within NaNh': a real defect the repoint removes); (b) BrandPoPreviewBody was Math.floor((orderDate + 24 * 3600 * 1000 - now) / 3600000) PLUS its own 'ack_overdue'/'ack_due' mapping and its own labels - it now derives its badge from the owner and the presentation layer, so the preview can no longer state a different window or vocabulary from the row; (c) THE ACTIONABILITY PREDICATE IS THE OWNER'S: 'actionable' was 'po.status === "received" || po.status === "under_review"' - the S3 defect class, which offered the brand an acceptance control PAST the 24-hour limit that the domain writer (src/data/api.ts -> acknowledgePurchaseOrder) REFUSES and treated an unreadable window as actionable - it is now poAcknowledgementWindow(po).inQueue (Amazon's New set INSIDE the window); (d) the on-behalf draft is no longer gated on canAct but on the OWNER's availability predicate, so past the limit - where an acceptance is refused and a rejection is the documented action - the brand is offered Mercenta's draft and approval, not a dead button. The acknowledgement panel additionally states the window the decision is made inside in the owner's own words (poAcknowledgementWindow(po).reason, data-testid po-ack-window-state-<poNumber>). (2) THE DELIVERED REMINDER'S OWN BRAND-SIDE DETAIL: the fan-out module gains the S6 view owner - poAckReminderViews(scope, tenantId) returns each delivered in-app reminder WITH every channel attempted for the same purchase order at the same declared stage (the refusals included), each carrying its label, state, destination, mode, simulated flag and reason, all read from the canonical ledger through the same tenant-scoped fail-closed accessors; poAckReminderChannelDetail(view) is the ONE sentence ('Email -> ops@... . In-app -> in-app (Mercenta-operated) . Instant message unavailable - <the fail-closed reason, verbatim>'). The notification centre consumes that view and renders the sentence as the item's own second line (meta, data-notification-meta) - and writes NONE of that copy itself (asserted at source level: no arrow sentence, no refusal copy in the centre's code). (3) THE STAGE-24 GATE WAS REPOINTED, NOT WEAKENED: scripts/validate-stage24.mjs asserted bpo.includes('24 * 60 * 60 * 1000') - it REQUIRED a second copy of the rule to exist, making the single-source-of-truth violation the test's success condition; it now asserts the opposite (the surface presents the window from the owner and re-derives nothing), with the old contract recorded inline and comments stripped for that assertion (the rules REQUIRE the repointed code to record the old contract inline). scripts/validate-po-acknowledgement-notifications.mjs's in-app-surface assertion was likewise repointed to the domain view that now wraps the same ledger accessor (old contract recorded inline). (4) NEW GATE: scripts/validate-po-acknowledgement-brand-surfaces.mjs (validate:po-ack-brand). (5) NEW FUNCTIONAL SPEC: e2e/po-brand-ack-surface.spec.ts (3 tests), plus the S5 spec gained the reminder's destination + refusal-reason assertions.

entries.description: PO-ACK S7 (2026-09-25, session 32) - THE ADMIN SURFACES PRESENT THE RULE FROM ITS ONE OWNER, AND A SIXTH COPY FOUND ON THE BRAND DASHBOARD IS REPOINTED TOO. Founder directive: the Amazon purchase-order process is a REPLICA of Amazon's documented rules; Mercenta invents nothing. The 24-hour rule was re-typed in SIX places (the S6 record named two). (1) AdminPurchaseOrderDetail.tsx derived the window on the surface: new Date(po.orderDate) mutated in LOCAL time by setHours(getHours() + 24) (drifting across a DST boundary), its own msLeft/hoursLeft/minutesLeft, its own isDeadlinePassed, its own 'EXPIRED' wording, its own header badge through a SECOND presentation helper, and its own actionability predicate (po.status !== 'received' && po.status !== 'under_review' - the S3/S6 defect class, which past the limit offered an ACCEPTANCE the domain writer REFUSES and rendered a countdown for an unreadable order date). It now reads poAcknowledgementWindow(po): the owner's reason is the badge's tooltip, ackHeaderBadge derives the badge from the owner's channelState (unknown -> 'Ack window unreadable'/ack_unknown FAIL-CLOSED; acknowledged -> 'Acknowledged'; closed -> the PO's own canonical status; new -> ackDeadlinePresentation's urgency plus 'closing window' when onBehalfAvailable), the deadline tile states the owner's classification instead of EXPIRED, the acceptance control is offered exactly when the owner's inQueue permits one, and when nothing is offered the surface STATES the owner's own reason (data-testid admin-po-ack-state-<poNumber>). (2) AdminPurchaseOrderList.tsx: the 'Awaiting action' figure was the same status predicate and the record preview hand-rolled Math.floor((orderDate + 24 * 3600 * 1000 - Date.now()) / 3600000) with Math.max(0, ...) clamps and a minutes term ((hoursLeft % 1) * 60) that is ALWAYS 0 once hoursLeft has been floored; both read the owner now and the preview badge is built exactly as the brand's (S6 parity). (3) AdminDashboard.tsx held a THIRD copy of the obligation set (PO_AWAITING = new Set(['received','under_review'])) driving the 'POs awaiting action' KPI ('Action needed' - a claim about ACTIONABILITY) and a FOURTH as its PO-pipeline bucket literal; the KPI reads the owner's inQueue and the bucket (a status-FAMILY view, stated as such in the code) reads the CONFIG array. (4) CommerceOperationsPanel.tsx's legitimate-next-actions flag and src/lib/commerce/commerceLifecycle.ts's domain guard read the config array (values unchanged). (5) The shared NotificationCenter.tsx's PO queue reads the owner (its rows stay tenant-scoped BEFORE the filter). (6) The demo seed read the predicate in TWO places; both now read the config array through ONE local derivation (the generated seed is unchanged). (7) THE SIXTH COPY, found by the same sweep and the worst of them, is BRAND side: src/components/brand/BrandDashboard.tsx's 'Awaiting acknowledgement' KPI ('Action needed', 'Acknowledge within 24 hours of receipt') hand-rolled the family AND its own unacknowledged-line rule and NEVER consulted the 24-hour window, so a purchase order past its limit was still counted as awaiting acknowledgement; it now reads the owner's inQueue. entries.description: PO-ACK S9 (2026-09-25, session 34) - RECEIPT -> INVOICE AUTOMATION. The stage row is the only written scope, so the contract was FIXED FROM THE REPOSITORY FIRST and recorded in the programme doc before implementation. WHAT WAS MISSING: the receipt and the invoice were TWO human actions with nothing between them - commerceLifecycle.receiveCommercePurchaseOrder logged the receipt (deriving the receiving status and auto-raising shortage deductions) and issueCommerceInvoice raised the invoice only when somebody pressed a button - and the receipt is the invoice's ONLY precondition, so the missing link WAS the stage. WHOSE RULE IT IS: the channel documents its invoice rules (AV-022) and documents invoicing a SHIPPED order; invoicing AFTER RECEIPT is Mercenta's own stricter rule (AV-018), so the automation is a MERCENTA operating decision and is LABELLED as Mercenta's, never as a channel rule. (1) THE ONE OWNER: NEW src/lib/commerce/receiptInvoiceAutomation.ts - the PURE decision (receiptInvoiceAutomationDecision: the TERMS are validated FIRST, then skip / refuse / issue), the write path with the canonical invoice writer INJECTED (applyReceiptInvoiceAutomation - the channelReceivingSync shape, so the module can never become a second way to raise an invoice), the declared automatic identity RECEIPT_INVOICE_AUTOMATION_ACTOR_ID = 'mercenta-system:receipt-invoice', the outcome codes (issue_on_receipt / already_invoiced / not_delivered / undeclared_terms / writer_refused), the statement RECEIPT_INVOICE_AUTOMATION_STATEMENT (headline, Mercenta's own process labelled, the terms basis DERIVED from invoiceTerms, the AV-022 correction, the simulation provenance) and the ONE surface wording receiptInvoiceAutomationSummary. No store, no clock, no randomness, no network. (2) THE RECEIPT IS THE TRIGGER: commerceLifecycle.receiveCommercePurchaseOrder gains an optional 4th argument carrying the terms (absent => the owner's DECLARED default, stated), runs the automation AFTER the receipt is recorded, and returns invoiceAutomation + invoice; the invoice goes through issueCommerceInvoice - the SAME canonical writer, so the receipt gate (AV-018), the number registry (AV-022), the zero-value refusal, the canonical trail and the derived due date are all unchanged. The trigger's own authorisation (RBAC + tenant isolation, enforced BEFORE the receipt) is what authorises the automatic issue. (3) ATTRIBUTION: issueCommerceInvoice gains automatedBy - the automatic issue is attributed to the declared automatic identity and NAMES the human trigger on BOTH canonical records ('Raised AUTOMATICALLY by mercenta-system:receipt-invoice (receipt by <actor>)'), the S2/S5 precedent, so the trail can never read as if somebody had issued the invoice by hand. (4) ONE NEW canonical activity type: invoice_automation_refused (src/types.ts), so a refusal is RECORDED rather than swallowed - the receipt stands (the goods arrived) while the invoice is not raised. (5) THE SURFACES: CommerceOperationsPanel chooses the terms AT THE RECEIPT (the select's enablement REPOINTED to 'while an invoice can still be raised', disabled once one is in force), passes them to the receipt, states the outcome from the owner's wording, renders the owner's statement (data-state admin-receipt-invoice-automation) and KEEPS the manual issue control as the fallback and AV-022's correction path (old contract recorded inline); CommerceSimulationPanel renders the same statement (data-state commerce-receipt-invoice-automation) and the same outcome wording. (6) REPOINTED CARRIERS (old contract recorded inline): e2e/invoicing.spec.ts (the terms are chosen BEFORE the receipt, which is what raises the invoice), e2e/admin-operational-surfaces.spec.ts, e2e/commerce-operational-simulation.spec.ts and e2e/deterministic-journey.spec.ts including its shared driveToDelivered helper. (7) TWO REAL REGRESSIONS THE EXISTING GATES FOUND, repointed never weakened: validate-e4-commerce's Q1/Q2/Q4 durable-write guarantee produced its invoice AFTER the conformance repository was injected - a write the automation now performs at the earlier receipt - so it now proves the guarantee through the S9 path itself (a PO received after the injection); and the E6/E7 change-scope guards gained the declared S9_RECEIPT_INVOICE_SCOPE / S9_RECEIPT_INVOICE_DECLARED surface with their contracts unchanged. entries.description: PUBLIC-MESSAGING BATCH B7 — THE STATIC PUBLIC SURFACE REBUILT ON THE OWNER'S FACTS. It was invisible because the browser checks render with JavaScript on (so <noscript> is never rendered) and validate:wording scans src/ only. NOW: the body noscript is a NOTICE (what the site is, enable JavaScript, the public contact address) and nothing else; the JSON-LD states only what can be evidenced in public and the SoftwareApplication node with its internal featureList is GONE rather than restated; ONE description is published in every place it appears (bootstrap meta, og:description, twitter:description and all three JSON-LD descriptions are asserted EQUAL to the SSOT home description, which is DERIVED from positioning.ts PUBLIC_PROMISE instead of retyped); /uk-market-access no longer publishes 'customs clearance' in its meta description; public/robots.txt no longer disallows /carrier for a surface P9 removed. entries.description: PUBLIC-MESSAGING BATCH B8 — THE CLAIMS GATE. src/config/positioning.ts §11 declares, as DATA, the eight families of claim a public surface may never make, and its own header said `scripts/validate-public-claims.mjs` compiles that list. FOR FOUR BATCHES IT DID NOT EXIST, so every red-line defect since was found BY HAND, one surface at a time: nine answers in the FAQ (B3), four claims across the two legal documents (B5), six engine-composed claims on the assessment result (B6) and an entire obsolete pre-B3 site inside index.html's noscript block (found by B6's live verification, fixed in B7). A rule with no gate is a rule that can be broken silently. THE GATE: it READS the eight declared families and their 48 patterns from the owner (never retyped, and NEVER SCANNED — the owner's block necessarily contains the phrases it forbids, so scanning it reports the gate's own definitions as violations, measured at nine), then scans WHAT A VISITOR OR CRAWLER RECEIVES: the published route titles and meta descriptions (8), the static public files delivered before any JavaScript runs (index.html IN FULL — a comment in a shipped file is published copy — plus robots.txt with its machine Allow/Disallow/Sitemap/Crawl-Delay lines stripped, because a path literal such as /api/ is a declared private prefix and not a claim, and sitemap.xml), and 18 RENDERED pages (every declared route in both shells, plus the assessment DRIVEN to its result because that copy is composed by the engine). IT FAILS CLOSED: below eight families or thirty patterns, on a short route list, on an empty scan, or when a render produced no text or threw an uncaught error, nothing is reported as clean.

entries.description: P1 OF THE CLEAN-UP/VERIFICATION PLAN — THE ONE SWITCH (2026-10-02). One environment owner decides whether the WHOLE platform runs in `demo` or `live`: src/config/environment.ts holds EnvironmentMode = 'demo' | 'live', reads the build default from VITE_ENVIRONMENT (anything but the exact value `live` means demo, so the demo host needs no variable), and keeps a runtime switch (remembered in localStorage, always winning over the build default). In `demo` the seed fallback returns seeded data and every provider stays simulated (no credential needed); in `live` the seed fallback returns NOTHING (a live platform can never serve a fake row) and an unconfigured provider resolves to `available` — UNAVAILABLE, NEVER simulation. The data layer's seed fallback is DEMO-ONLY; the provider-mode machine (modeForState) reads the owner; the switch is operable in ONE obvious place (the Simulation Control Centre). The fail-closed isProviderSimulationSafe rule is UNCHANGED.

entries.description: E2E-0 (2026-10-04; formerly §BATCH 0 — RENAMED 2026-10-04 to end a name collision with the build 'Batches') — THE E2E SCENARIO CATALOGUE + TRACEABILITY GATE. The end-to-end suite must cover EVERY scenario for the ENTIRE platform, and that must be MACHINE-HELD rather than claimed. ONE owner of the scenario list, `docs/scenario-catalogue.json`, holds the scenario list plus the METHOD (the eight axes — object · actor · trigger · outcome · data_condition · tenancy · provider_mode · time — whose cross-product with an object lifecycle defines the space). `scripts/e2e-catalogue.mjs` seeds it from the existing specs (`--seed`) and projects it to the GENERATED document `docs/WHOLE_PLATFORM_E2E_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md` (`--doc`); `scripts/validate-e2e-scenarios.mjs` is the GATE (swept automatically by `npm run validate:all`, because the corpus globs `scripts/validate-*.mjs`). The gate fails if: the catalogue is malformed; a scenario names a spec that does not exist (missing test); a capability has no scenario; a scenario id is duplicated; an e2e spec is named by NO scenario (orphan test); or the generated doc has DRIFTED from the owner. Seeded at 95 scenarios across 8 capability families (one per existing spec). The catalogue owner deliberately lives in `docs/` so it is OUTSIDE the product-source scans and the E6 F6 source-scope. No application runtime change — a validator, a generator, a catalogue and npm scripts only.

entries.description: DISCOVERED (2026-10-05, this session) while fixing `discovered-adminshell-chunk-size`: the SAME defect existed in the BRAND portal shell. `BrandShell` eagerly imported all 24 brand view panels, so they all landed in ONE ~637 kB `BrandShell-*.js` chunk and a brand downloaded every panel to open any one of them. entries.description: E2E-8 (2026-10-08) — DEFECT FIXED AT SOURCE (rule 07). While enumerating the integrations domain, `e2e/embedded-social.spec.ts` was found FLAKY under parallel load: tests 4 and 5 read the Social workspace id IMMEDIATELY after a brand switch (`expect(await workspaceId(page)).toBe(before)` with NO wait), so either could sample the MID-SWITCH tenant; the poll budget was only 10s and the whole test sat on Playwright 30s default. Observed: tests 5 and 6 failing intermittently at 8 workers. FIX AT SOURCE: the three immediate assertions now GO THROUGH the spec own wait helper — which is only satisfiable by the app genuinely returning to that tenant, because the id is `msoc-${stableHash(tenantId)}`, a deterministic function of the tenant alone — and the budgets are raised (polls 40s, per-test 120s). NO assertion was changed or removed. The changed test file is declared in BOTH scope guards (E6 + E7), mirroring the E2E-4 record-drawer precedent. HONEST LIMIT (not hidden): under this machine AMBIENT load from several UNRELATED projects (multiple Vite dev servers + another project Playwright run were observed), the switch can still exceed the budget and the spec can fail (~1 of 6 local runs); it passes reliably in isolation. The PRODUCT is correct — the surface always shows the CURRENT session own workspace and the cross-tenant assertions never leaked — so this is test-load sensitivity, not a product defect, and the affected test must not be reported as reliably passing under ambient load.

E6 PASS · E7 PASS (121/0) · `validate:all` 188 PASS / 0 FAIL · typecheck 0 · build ✓. The spec runs green in isolation (1/1) and 19/19 in 5 of 6 consecutive parallel runs; the residual 1/6 is the disclosed ambient-load sensitivity. Non-runtime governance increment => three-way NOT APPLICABLE.

entries.description: E2E-8 (2026-10-08) — DEFECT FIXED AT SOURCE (rule 07). While closing the session, `git add -A` COMMITTED a 4.5 MB GENERATED artefact: an Info-ZIP transient temp file (`Review Zip/ziePvPew`) left beside the archive by the review-zip export. `.gitignore` only ignored `Review Zip/*.zip`, so the temp file was NOT ignored (git never reads the export script, so the ignore is the only defence). VERIFIED SAFE BEFORE FIXING: the committed blob was extracted and inspected — it contains NO `.env` entry and no gitignored tree, so no secret left the machine. FIXED: (a) the file is UNTRACKED; (b) `.gitignore` now ignores EVERYTHING under `Review Zip/` except the intentionally-tracked `INCIDENT-LOG.md`; (c) a GATE was added to `scripts/validate-production-hygiene.mjs` §D that FAILS if git tracks anything under `Review Zip/` other than `INCIDENT-LOG.md`, or if the ignore rule loses its broad form. E6 declares `.gitignore` as a changed file. HONEST LIMIT: the 4.5 MB blob remains in the PUSHED git HISTORY (rewriting history needs a force-push, which the project forbids); it is inert and secret-free, and no future occurrence is possible.
entries.source: Discovered by the mandatory clean-tree check at task close; fixed in the same session per rule 07 (fix defects at source, never park a fixable defect).
entries.evidence: `git ls-files -- "Review Zip"` now lists ONLY `Review Zip/INCIDENT-LOG.md`; `.gitignore` carries `Review Zip/*` + `!Review Zip/INCIDENT-LOG.md`. GATE MUTATION-PROVED TWICE — (A) force-tracking a dummy `Review Zip/ziMUTANT` ⇒ the tracked-artefact assertion FAILS (PRODUCTION_HYGIENE_FAIL 4/5); (B) narrowing `.gitignore` back to `Review Zip/*.zip` ⇒ the ignore-rule assertion FAILS (4/5); each restored and re-run ⇒ PASS 5/5. E6 PASS (the `.gitignore` change is declared) · E7 PASS (121/0) · `validate:all` 188 PASS / 0 FAIL. Non-runtime governance increment => three-way NOT APPLICABLE.
